info.description:
# RetailStore_2n API

Every endpoint of the RetailStore_2n Express API (145 requests), grouped the way people use them: browsing, buying, selling, and running the shop. Each request carries its own documentation: who may call it, the body fields and their rules, the possible responses and error codes, and the source file it lives in.

The full written reference is `docs/api.md` in the repository. Where it and this collection differ, this collection follows the code.

## Getting started

1. Start the stack locally (see the repository README). The API listens on `http://localhost:4000`.
2. Import this collection and `RetailStore_2n.local.postman_environment.json`, then select the **RetailStore_2n — Local** environment.
3. Run **Health › Liveness**. It should return `200 {"status":"ok"}`.
4. Run **Auth › Signup & login › Sign up** (or **Log in** if the account already exists).

From then on, requests that need a login just work: see *How login works* below.

## How login works

The API uses cookies, not tokens in headers.

- Logging in (or signing up) sets two httpOnly cookies: `retailstore_2n_access` (15 minutes) and `retailstore_2n_refresh` (30 days).
- Postman's cookie jar stores them for `localhost` and sends them with every later request. You do not need to copy anything.
- When the access cookie expires you get `401`. Run **Auth › Session › Refresh session**, or log in again.
- **One session at a time.** The cookie jar holds one login per host. To act as a different user (for example a buyer, then a seller), run **Log out**, change `email`, and log in again.

Email verification is currently **switched off**: signup creates a verified account and signs it in straight away.

## Variables

- **Inputs** you may change: `baseUrl`, `email`, `password`, `newPassword`, `adminPassword`, `phone`, `totpCode`.
- **Saved automatically**: ids such as `listingId`, `orderId`, `addressId`. A request's test script saves them from its response, so the next request can use them. Each request's description lists what it **needs** and what it **saves**.

## A full walkthrough

Use two accounts, a seller and a buyer.

**As the seller**

1. Sign up (`email` = seller address) → **Auth › Seller onboarding › Become a seller**.
2. **Catalog › List categories** (saves `categoryId`).
3. **Seller › Listings › Create listing** (saves `listingId`) → **Listing images › Upload listing photo** (pick a JPEG/PNG/WebP file in the Body tab) → **Publish listing**.
4. Optional, for payouts: **Identity verification › Start verification session** → **Submit document (stub only)** (see test values) → **Payouts › Start payout account onboarding** → **Complete stub onboarding**.

**As the buyer** (log out, change `email`, sign up)

5. **Buyer › Addresses › Create address**.
6. **Reservations (cart holds) › Hold a listing (add to cart)** → **Orders & checkout › Checkout (create order from holds)** (saves `orderId`) → **Pay for an order** with card `4242424242424242`.

**Back as the seller**: **Seller › Sales › List my sales** (saves `orderItemId`) → **Mark sale shipped**.

**Back as the buyer**: **Buyer › Orders & checkout › Confirm item delivered**.

## Test values

These work with the default stub providers; nothing real is charged, checked or sent.

| What | Value | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Card | `4242424242424242` (or any number not listed below) | Paid |
| Card | `4000000000000002` | Declined (HTTP 200, `outcome: "failed"`, order closes) |
| Card | `4000000000000069` | Expired card (order closes) |
| Card | `4000000000000119` | Processing error (order closes) |
| Card | `4000002500003155` | Needs 3-D Secure (`outcome: "pending"`) |
| Identity document number | ends in `0000` | Rejected: image unreadable |
| Identity document number | ends in `0001` | Rejected: name mismatch |
| Identity document number | anything else, e.g. `X12345678` | Verified |
| SMS code | returned as `devCode` by the stub SMS provider | Verifies the phone |

A failed card closes the order and releases the item, so reserve and check out again before retrying. Stub payment intents and stub payout accounts live in the API's memory and are lost when the API restarts.

## Admin access (one-time setup)

Admin routes need a role **and** a separate short admin session.

1. Grant the role from a shell: `cd backend && npm run admin:grant -- you@example.com`. There is no HTTP route for this.
2. Log in as that user, then **Admin › Admin session (TOTP & step-up) › Start TOTP enrolment** with your password. Add the returned `secret` to an authenticator app.
3. **Confirm TOTP enrolment** with the current code in `totpCode`.
4. **Step up into admin session** with `adminPassword` and a fresh `totpCode`. This sets the `retailstore_2n_admin` cookie for 30 minutes. Repeat this step when it expires.

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{ "error": "Human-readable message", "code": "MACHINE_CODE", "field": "priceCents" }`. `field` is present when one input is at fault; `code` is stable, `error` text is not.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 400 | Validation failed |
| 401 | No or expired session |
| 403 | Signed in but not allowed (`NOT_A_SELLER`, `PAYOUTS_LOCKED`) |
| 404 | Not found, **also returned for records owned by someone else** |
| 409 | Conflicts with the current state |
| 429 | Rate limited |

Money is in whole minor units (`priceCents`), except the `minPrice`/`maxPrice` filters on **Catalog › List listings**, which are whole currency units.

## Running it as a test suite

Each request checks its expected status code. The Collection Runner can run a folder in order. Some requests change state for good (becoming a seller, signing up the same email twice, reporting the same thing twice, changing the password), so run against a local database you can re-seed.

**Auth:** None — public.

Reports whether notification consumers are keeping up. Kept separate from `/health` because it talks to the Kafka broker over the network. On the inline transport (no Kafka configured) it always answers `{ transport: "inline", healthy: true, relayInProcess, detail }`. On Kafka it returns `{ transport: "kafka", healthy, groups: [{ group, lag, byTopic, uncommitted }], dlqDepth, thresholds: { lag, dlq }, missingTopics?, error? }`. Lag covers every retry-ladder topic, not just the main one. **503 when unhealthy**, so a monitor need not parse the body.

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Healthy (inline transport, or Kafka lag/DLQ under thresholds) |  |
| 503 | Unhealthy: lag or DLQ over threshold, broker unreachable, or the report itself threw ({ healthy: false, error }) |  |

_Source: `backend/src/index.ts:96`_

request.description:
**Auth:** None — public.

Creates an account. **Email verification is currently switched off**: the account is created with `emailVerified: true`, both auth cookies (`retailstore_2n_access`, `retailstore_2n_refresh`) are set, and `201 { user }` is returned. No verification email is sent. Signing up again on an existing *unverified* email updates its name/password and verifies it; on an existing *verified* email it is a 409, so re-running this request with the same email fails. No rate limit. Note: error responses here carry `error` and `field` but **no `code`**.

**Needs variables:** `email`, `password` — set by an earlier request.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | yes | trimmed, min 1, max 100 |
| `email` | string | yes | trimmed, lower-cased, email format |
| `password` | string | yes | min 12 chars; also rejected if found in Pwned Passwords breach corpus |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 201 | Account created and signed in: { user: { id, name, email, isSeller, emailVerified, avatarUrl, createdAt } }; sets both cookies |  |
| 400 | Validation failed (first zod issue message; field = name\|email\|password), or password found in a breach (field = password) |  |
| 409 | An account with that email already exists and is verified (field = email) |  |

**Saves:** `userId` ← `user.id`

request.description:
**Auth:** None — public.

Signs in and sets both auth cookies. **Rate limited to 10 attempts per 15 minutes per submitted email address** (fails open if Redis is down); the counter clears on a correct password. Wrong email and wrong password give the same 401. Suspension is checked only after the password is proven. Because verification is switched off, unverified accounts may log in (no `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`). There is no per-IP limit.

**Needs variables:** `email`, `password` — set by an earlier request.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | yes | trimmed, lower-cased, email format |
| `password` | string | yes | min 1 |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Signed in: { user: { id, name, email, isSeller, emailVerified, avatarUrl, createdAt } }; sets both cookies |  |
| 400 | Validation failed ({ error, field }, no code) |  |
| 401 | Incorrect email or password | `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` |
| 403 | Account suspended (message includes the reason if set) | `ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED` |
| 429 | Too many attempts for this address; body has retryAfterSeconds | `RATE_LIMITED` |

**Saves:** `userId` ← `user.id`

_Source: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts:133`_

**Auth:** Signed-in user (cookies from **Auth › Signup & login › Log in**).

Rotates the refresh token (read from the `retailstore_2n_refresh` cookie) and issues a new access cookie. Needs only the refresh cookie, not a valid access token. Reusing an already-rotated token revokes the whole token family, except within a ~10 second grace window after rotation, where a racing request gets a new access cookie but no new refresh cookie. On an expired/revoked token the cookies are cleared.

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 204 | New access cookie (and normally a new refresh cookie) set; empty body |  |
| 401 | No refresh cookie ('Not authenticated'), or session expired/revoked ('Session expired, please log in again'; cookies cleared) |  |

_Source: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts:321`_

**Auth:** None — public.

Revokes the refresh token from the cookie (if present) and clears both auth cookies. Always 204, even with no session. Run it last: every authenticated request after it returns 401 until you log in again.

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 204 | Signed out; cookies cleared; empty body |  |

request.description:
**Auth:** None — public.

Redeems an email verification token and signs the user in (sets both cookies). The token only arrives by email (or the backend console with `MAIL_TRANSPORT=console`); it is never returned by any API response. **While verification is switched off, signup sends no email, so there is normally no token to use** and this request will return 400.

**Needs variables:** `verificationToken` — set by an earlier request.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | string | yes | min 1; single-use token from the emailed link (24h expiry per docs) |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | Verified and signed in: { user } |  |
| 400 | Missing token, or the link is invalid/expired (no code) |  |

**Saves:** `userId` ← `user.id`

_Source: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts:280`_

**Auth:** None — public.

Sends a fresh verification link if the account exists and is unverified. Returns the same 200 message whether or not the account exists or is already verified, so it cannot be used to probe emails. A malformed email gets a 400 (unlike `/auth/password/forgot`). No rate limit in the route. With verification switched off, accounts are created verified, so this is effectively a no-op.

**Needs variables:** `email` — set by an earlier request.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | yes | trimmed, lower-cased, email format |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { message: "If that email needs verification, we've sent a new link." } |  |
| 400 | Not a valid email (no code) |  |

_Source: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts:303`_

**Auth:** Signed-in user (cookies from **Auth › Signup & login › Log in**).

Changes the password of a signed-in user; the current password is required even with a valid session. Revokes every **other** refresh token (this session survives) and burns outstanding reset links. **Rate limited to 10 per 15 minutes per user.** Side effect: after this, `{{password}}` no longer works, so swap `password` and `newPassword` before logging in again.

**Needs variables:** `password`, `newPassword` — set by an earlier request.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `currentPassword` | string | yes | min 1; must match the current password |
| `newPassword` | string | yes | zod min 1; service then requires >= 12 chars, different from current, and not in a breach corpus |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { ok: true, otherSessionsEnded, message } |  |
| 400 | Missing field, or new password under 12 chars (field = newPassword) | `INVALID_INPUT` |
| 400 | New password equals the current one | `SAME_PASSWORD` |
| 400 | New password found in breach corpus | `PASSWORD_BREACHED` |
| 401 | Not signed in (no code), or current password wrong (field = currentPassword) | `WRONG_PASSWORD` |
| 404 | Account not found | `NOT_FOUND` |
| 429 | Too many attempts; body has retryAfterSeconds | `RATE_LIMITED` |

_Source: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts:383`_

**Auth:** None — public.

Requests a password reset link by email. **Always 200 with the same body**, whether the address is registered, unregistered, malformed, rate limited, or the send failed, so it is not an enumeration oracle. **Rate limited silently: 3/hour per address and 20/hour per caller IP**; when limited, no email is sent but the response is unchanged. A new request invalidates any earlier unused link. The token arrives only by email (or the backend console with `MAIL_TRANSPORT=console`).

**Needs variables:** `email` — set by an earlier request.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | yes | trimmed, lower-cased, email format (a malformed value still gets the same 200) |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { message: "If that address has an account, a reset link is on its way." } |  |

_Source: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts:435`_

**Auth:** None — public.

Redeems a reset token and sets a new password. Revokes **every** session, marks the email verified, and clears the auth cookies; **no session is issued**, so log in again afterwards. Unknown, expired and used tokens all give the same `INVALID_TOKEN`. **Rate limited to 100/hour per caller IP** (the 429 here has no retryAfterSeconds). The token is never returned by the API; copy it from the email or backend console into `resetToken`.

**Needs variables:** `resetToken`, `newPassword` — set by an earlier request.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | string | yes | min 1; single-use, 1 hour expiry, from the emailed link |
| `newPassword` | string | yes | zod min 1; service then requires >= 12 chars, different from current, and not in a breach corpus |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { ok: true, message: "Password changed. Sign in with your new password." }; cookies cleared |  |
| 400 | Missing field, or new password under 12 chars | `INVALID_INPUT` |
| 400 | Token unknown, expired or already used | `INVALID_TOKEN` |
| 400 | New password equals the current one | `SAME_PASSWORD` |
| 400 | New password found in breach corpus | `PASSWORD_BREACHED` |
| 429 | Too many attempts from this IP | `RATE_LIMITED` |

_Source: `backend/src/routes/auth.ts:476`_

Turns the signed-in user into a seller: sets `isSeller: true` and creates a `SellerProfile` (shopName defaults to the user's name) in one transaction. Idempotent; calling it again changes nothing. | --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { user } with isSeller: true |  |
| 401 | Not authenticated |  |

request.description:
**Auth:** Signed-in user (cookies from **Auth › Signup & login › Log in**).

Sets the profile picture. Send `multipart/form-data` with one file in field `avatar`. The image is cropped to a square, re-encoded to WebP (EXIF stripped), written to storage, and only its URL is stored. The old picture is deleted only after the new URL is saved. **Rate limited to 10 uploads per user per hour** (checked before the file is inspected). In Postman, pick a local image file for the `avatar` field.

### Body
| Field | Type | Required | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `avatar` | file | yes | single file; max 5 MB (MAX_AVATAR_BYTES); JPEG, PNG or WebP checked by magic bytes |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { user: { id, name, email, isSeller, emailVerified, avatarUrl, createdAt } } with the new avatarUrl |  |
| 400 | Over 5 MB or unreadable multipart upload | `UPLOAD_FAILED` |
| 400 | No file attached | `NO_FILE` |
| 400 | Not a real JPEG/PNG/WebP, empty, or could not be processed | `INVALID_IMAGE` |
| 401 | Not authenticated |  |
| 404 | Account not found |  |
| 429 | Hourly cap hit; body has retryAfterSeconds | `RATE_LIMITED` |

_Source: `backend/src/routes/profile.ts:55`_

**Auth:** Signed-in user (cookies from **Auth › Signup & login › Log in**).

Lists reviews written by the signed-in user, newest first, up to 50. Each item: `{ id, rating, body, createdAt, edited, listing: { slug, title, priceCents, currency, image, available } }`. `available` is false when the listing was deleted or removed. An account with no reviews gets an empty list. Not documented in docs/api.md.

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { reviews: [...] } |  |
| 401 | Not authenticated |  |
| 500 | Could not load your reviews |  |

_Source: `backend/src/routes/profile.ts:114`_

request.description:
**Auth:** None — public.

Paged search over ACTIVE, non-deleted listings. Empty-string params are treated as absent. Response: `{ listings, total, page, limit, pageCount }`; each listing is `{ id, slug, title, description, condition, conditionNote, priceCents, originalPriceCents, currency, quantity, status, featured, createdAt, isNew, category: { slug, title }, seller: { shopName, verified }, images: [{ url, alt, position }], rating: { average | null, count } }`. Filter params are disabled by default so the first listing can be captured.

### Query
| Param | Example | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | jacket | no | Case-insensitive substring of title or description; trimmed, max 120 |
| `category` | {{categorySlug}} | no | Category slug; trimmed, max 64 |
| `condition` | LIKE_NEW | no | One of LIKE_NEW \| GOOD \| WELL_LOVED \| NEEDS_REPAIR |
| `minPrice` | 10 | no | Whole currency units (not cents); 0 to 1,000,000; must be <= maxPrice |
| `maxPrice` | 500 | no | Whole currency units (not cents); 0 to 1,000,000 |
| `featured` | true | no | "true" or "false" |
| `sort` | newest | no | newest (default) \| price_asc \| price_desc |
| `page` | 1 | no | Integer 1 to 500; default 1 |
| `limit` | 24 | no | Integer 1 to 48; default 24 |

### Responses
| Status | Meaning | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { listings, total, page, limit, pageCount } |  |
| 400 | A param failed validation | `INVALID_QUERY` |
| 400 | minPrice > maxPrice (field = minPrice) | `INVALID_PRICE_RANGE` |
| 500 | Could not load listings |  |

**Saves:** `listingId` ← `listings[0].id`, `listingSlug` ← `listings[0].slug`

**Auth:** None — public.

| --- | --- | --- |
| 200 | { listing, related } |  |
| 404 | Slug unknown, deleted, or not ACTIVE/RESERVED/SOLD | `NOT_FOUND` |
